problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Shipment Alpha: size 36 cubic meters
* Shipment Beta: size 53 cubic meters
* Shipment Gamma: size 44 cubic meters
* Shipment Delta: size 37 cubic meters
* Shipment Epsilon: size 50 cubic meters
* Shipment Zeta: size 38 cubic meters
* Shipment Eta: size 42 cubic meters
* Shipment Theta: size 45 cubic meters
* Shipment Iota: size 69 cubic meters
* Shipment Kappa: size 65 cubic meters
* Shipment Lambda: size 50 cubic meters
* Shipment Mu: size 61 cubic meters
* Shipment Nu: size 51 cubic meters
* Shipment Xi: size 67 cubic meters
* Shipment Omicron: size 70 cubic meters
* Shipment Pi: size 60 cubic meters
* Shipment Rho: size 62 cubic meters
* Shipment Sigma: size 47 cubic meters
* Shipment Tau: size 48 cubic meters
* Shipment Upsilon: size 31 cubic meters
* Shipment Phi: size 69 cubic meters
* Shipment Chi: size 69 cubic meters
* Shipment Psi: size 41 cubic meters
* Shipment Omega: size 47 cubic meters
* Shipment A1: size 42 cubic meters
* Shipment B1: size 62 cubic meters
* Shipment C1: size 65 cubic meters
* Shipment D1: size 37 cubic meters
* Shipment E1: size 49 cubic meters
* Shipment F1: size 58 cubic meters

Each cargo plane has a maximum capacity of 100 cubic meters. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes. Each shipment must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume in a plane cannot exceed its capacity.
